transforms.name: accusative
transforms.description: Accusative -n: the direct object, or the direction of motion. domon → domo, belan → bela, domojn → domoj, hejmen → hejme, kien → kie, kion → kio, min → mi, kiun → kiu.

transforms.name: plural
transforms.description: Plural -j of nouns and adjectives. domoj → domo, belaj → bela, kiuj → kiu, miaj → mia.

transforms.name: present
transforms.description: Present tense -as: mi legas (I read, I am reading) → legi.

transforms.name: past
transforms.description: Past tense -is: mi legis (I read, I was reading) → legi.

transforms.name: future
transforms.description: Future tense -os: mi legos (I will read) → legi.

transforms.name: conditional
transforms.description: Conditional -us: mi legus (I would read) → legi.

transforms.name: volitive
transforms.description: Volitive -u, the imperative and the wish: legu! (read!), ke mi legu (that I should read) → legi.

transforms.name: present active participle
transforms.description: -anta, the present active participle as an adjective: legi → leganta (reading), leganto (reader, one who is reading), legante (while reading).

transforms.name: present active participle (noun)
transforms.description: -anto, the present active participle as a noun: legi → leganta (reading), leganto (reader, one who is reading), legante (while reading).

transforms.name: present active participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -ante, the present active participle as an adverb: legi → leganta (reading), leganto (reader, one who is reading), legante (while reading).

transforms.name: past active participle
transforms.description: -inta, the past active participle as an adjective: legi → leginta (having read), leginto (one who has read), leginte (having read).

transforms.name: past active participle (noun)
transforms.description: -into, the past active participle as a noun: legi → leginta (having read), leginto (one who has read), leginte (having read).

transforms.name: past active participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -inte, the past active participle as an adverb: legi → leginta (having read), leginto (one who has read), leginte (having read).

transforms.name: future active participle
transforms.description: -onta, the future active participle as an adjective: legi → legonta (about to read), legonto (one who will read), legonte (being about to read).

transforms.name: future active participle (noun)
transforms.description: -onto, the future active participle as a noun: legi → legonta (about to read), legonto (one who will read), legonte (being about to read).

transforms.name: future active participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -onte, the future active participle as an adverb: legi → legonta (about to read), legonto (one who will read), legonte (being about to read).

transforms.name: present passive participle
transforms.description: -ata, the present passive participle as an adjective: legi → legata (being read), legato (one who is being read), legate (while being read).

transforms.name: present passive participle (noun)
transforms.description: -ato, the present passive participle as a noun: legi → legata (being read), legato (one who is being read), legate (while being read).

transforms.name: present passive participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -ate, the present passive participle as an adverb: legi → legata (being read), legato (one who is being read), legate (while being read).

transforms.name: past passive participle
transforms.description: -ita, the past passive participle as an adjective: legi → legita (read, having been read), legito (one who has been read), legite (having been read).

transforms.name: past passive participle (noun)
transforms.description: -ito, the past passive participle as a noun: legi → legita (read, having been read), legito (one who has been read), legite (having been read).

transforms.name: past passive participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -ite, the past passive participle as an adverb: legi → legita (read, having been read), legito (one who has been read), legite (having been read).

transforms.name: future passive participle
transforms.description: -ota, the future passive participle as an adjective: legi → legota (to be read), legoto (one who will be read), legote (being about to be read).

transforms.name: future passive participle (noun)
transforms.description: -oto, the future passive participle as a noun: legi → legota (to be read), legoto (one who will be read), legote (being about to be read).

transforms.name: future passive participle (adverb)
transforms.description: -ote, the future passive participle as an adverb: legi → legota (to be read), legoto (one who will be read), legote (being about to be read).

transforms.name: elision
transforms.description: Elided article: l' → la. (The elided -o of a noun is the processor elision: dank' → danko.)

transforms.name: -ad- (continued action)
transforms.description: Continued or repeated action: kurado (running) → kuri, venadis → venadi → veni.

transforms.name: -aĉ- (pejorative)
transforms.description: Poor or contemptible: domaĉo (hovel) → domo, skribaĉi (to scribble) → skribi.

transforms.name: -aĵ- (thing)
transforms.description: A concrete thing made, done or having a quality: manĝaĵo (food) → manĝi, novaĵo (news) → nova, bovaĵo (beef) → bovo.

transforms.name: -an- (member)
transforms.description: Member, follower or inhabitant: klubano → klubo, urbano → urbo.

transforms.name: -ar- (group)
transforms.description: A collection: arbaro (forest) → arbo, vortaro (dictionary) → vorto.

transforms.name: -ebl- (possible)
transforms.description: Possible to: farebla (feasible) → fari, kompreneble (of course) → kompreni.

transforms.name: -ec- (quality)
transforms.description: The quality or state: beleco (beauty) → bela, infaneco (childhood) → infano.

transforms.name: -eg- (augmentative)
transforms.description: Large or intense: domego → domo, grandega → granda, ridegi → ridi, bonege → bone.

transforms.name: -ej- (place)
transforms.description: The place for: lernejo (school) → lerni, kafejo (café) → kafo.

transforms.name: -em- (inclined to)
transforms.description: Inclined to: laborema (hard-working) → labori, dormema (sleepy) → dormi.

transforms.name: -end- (to be done)
transforms.description: Must be done: pagenda (payable) → pagi, legenda (to be read) → legi.

transforms.name: -estr- (leader)
transforms.description: The head of: lernejestro (headmaster) → lernejo, urbestro (mayor) → urbo.

transforms.name: -et- (diminutive)
transforms.description: Small or weak: dometo → domo, beleta → bela, rideti (to smile) → ridi.

transforms.name: -id- (offspring)
transforms.description: The young or descendant: katido (kitten) → kato, bovido (calf) → bovo.

transforms.name: -ig- (cause)
transforms.description: To make, to cause to be or do: purigi (to clean) → pura, mortigi (to kill) → morti.

transforms.name: -iĝ- (become)
transforms.description: To become, to get: ruĝiĝi (to blush) → ruĝa, leviĝi (to rise) → levi, edziĝi (to marry) → edzo.

transforms.name: -il- (tool)
transforms.description: The tool for: tranĉilo (knife) → tranĉi, ludilo (toy) → ludi.

transforms.name: -in- (female)
transforms.description: Female: patrino (mother) → patro, reĝino (queen) → reĝo, katino → kato.

transforms.name: -ind- (worthy)
transforms.description: Worthy of: laŭdinda (praiseworthy) → laŭdi, vidinda → vidi.

transforms.name: -ist- (professional)
transforms.description: A person occupied with: dentisto (dentist) → dento, kudristo (tailor) → kudri.

transforms.name: -uj- (container)
transforms.description: Container, tree or country: sukerujo (sugar bowl) → sukero, pomujo → pomo.

transforms.name: -ul- (person)
transforms.description: A person characterised by: junulo (young person) → juna, riĉulo → riĉa.

transforms.name: adverb
transforms.description: The adverb of a root whose adjective, noun or verb is the headword: rigide (rigidly) → rigida, kaŭze (because of) → kaŭzo, konsente (in agreement) → konsenti.

transforms.name: word class
transforms.description: Another word class of the same root, when a request turns it on: lana (woollen) → lano, skriba (written) → skribi, eldiro (utterance) → eldiri.

transforms.name: mal- (opposite)
transforms.description: The opposite: malbona (bad) → bona, malfermi (to open) → fermi, malsupren → supren.

transforms.name: ne- (not)
transforms.description: Not: nejuna → juna, nekonata (unknown) → konata.

transforms.name: re- (again, back)
transforms.description: Again or back: reveni (to come back) → veni, relegi → legi.

transforms.name: ek- (beginning)
transforms.description: Beginning or sudden action: ekridi (to burst out laughing) → ridi, ekvidi → vidi.

transforms.name: dis- (apart)
transforms.description: Apart, in all directions: disiri (to part) → iri, disĵeti → ĵeti.

transforms.name: for- (away)
transforms.description: Away: foriri (to leave) → iri, forkuri → kuri.

transforms.name: el- (out)
transforms.description: Out, thoroughly: eliri (to go out) → iri, elpensi (to devise) → pensi.

transforms.name: en- (in)
transforms.description: In, into: eniri (to enter) → iri, enkuri → kuri.

transforms.name: kun- (together)
transforms.description: Together: kunveni (to meet) → veni, kunlabori → labori, kunsento (sympathy) → sento.

transforms.name: al- (to)
transforms.description: To, towards: aliri (to approach) → iri, aldoni (to add) → doni.

transforms.name: antaŭ- (before)
transforms.description: Before: antaŭdiri (to predict) → diri, antaŭvidi → vidi.

transforms.name: ĉe- (at)
transforms.description: At: ĉeesti (to attend) → esti.

transforms.name: ĉirkaŭ- (around)
transforms.description: Around: ĉirkaŭvolvi (to wrap around) → volvi, ĉirkaŭrigardi → rigardi.

transforms.name: de- (from, off)
transforms.description: From, off: defali (to fall off) → fali, depreni (to take away) → preni.

transforms.name: inter- (between)
transforms.description: Between, mutually: intermiksi (to intermix) → miksi, interŝanĝi → ŝanĝi.

transforms.name: kontraŭ- (against)
transforms.description: Against: kontraŭstari (to oppose) → stari.

transforms.name: per- (by means of)
transforms.description: Achieved by: perlabori (to earn) → labori.

transforms.name: post- (after)
transforms.description: After, behind: postlasi (to leave behind) → lasi.

transforms.name: preter- (past)
transforms.description: Past, beyond: preterpasi (to pass by) → pasi, preterŝoviĝi → ŝoviĝi.

transforms.name: pri- (about)
transforms.description: About, making a verb transitive: prikalkuli (to calculate) → kalkuli, priskribi (to describe) → skribi.

transforms.name: sub- (under)
transforms.description: Under: submeti (to submit) → meti, subskribi (to sign) → skribi.

transforms.name: super- (over)
transforms.description: Over: superŝuti (to shower) → ŝuti.

transforms.name: sur- (on)
transforms.description: On: surmeti (to put on) → meti, surpaŝi → paŝi.

transforms.name: tra- (through)
transforms.description: Through: trabati (to pierce) → bati, travivi (to live through) → vivi.

transforms.name: trans- (across)
transforms.description: Across: transkuri (to run across) → kuri, transdoni (to hand over) → doni.

transforms.name: ge- (both sexes)
transforms.description: Both sexes together: gepatroj (parents) → patroj, gefratoj → fratoj.

transforms.name: pra- (primordial)
transforms.description: Primordial, of an earlier generation: praavo (great-grandfather) → avo, prahomo → homo.

transforms.name: mis- (wrongly)
transforms.description: Wrongly: miskompreni (to misunderstand) → kompreni.

transforms.name: sen- (without)
transforms.description: Without: senforta (weak) → forto, senbrue (noiselessly) → bruo, senkulpa (innocent) → kulpo.
